edges.finding: Rijnstate appears as Velp in NCT04627974 and as Arnhem/Rijnstate Hospital or Rijnstate ziekenhuis in the other three. The registrations involve different sponsors, indications or protocols; no common participant identifiers or re-enrollment statement were found in these records.

primary_publication_review_2026_09_27.primary_locators: Methods, Study design and Statistics/Secondary objectives; Results, Subject disposition; Table 2; ClinicalTrials.gov resultsSection.outcomeMeasuresModule for NCT05177354
primary_publication_review_2026_09_27.verified_disposition: 94 enrolled, 75 trialed, 60 implanted and 54 completed the three-month visit. The randomized, blinded crossover compared CL versus OL only for in-clinic overstimulation, 25/28 improved at one month. Three-month pain response was a separate single-arm secondary endpoint: 44/51 overall low-back/leg, 38/43 low-back and 30/41 leg achieved at least 50% VAS reduction. Registry aggregate counts and article percentages agree.
primary_publication_review_2026_09_27.boundary: This publication and NCT05177354 describe the same cohort. No long-term randomized pain comparison, individual ECAP-to-pain dataset, ECAP-based pain predictor or external predictive validation is established; registry IPD=NO.

existing_record_correction.finding: Registry places VAS pain in primary outcomes, Ashworth/SF-36/medication/EQ-5D in secondary outcomes, and ECAP morphology/current/conduction velocity in other outcomes; corrected contradictory boundary and audit field.

search_update.boundary: Two additional registrations were added: CIPRESS explicitly links ECAP-controlled CL-SCS intent to longitudinal NRS pain outcomes but has no results/IPD release; NCT07780032 is a distinct RLS indication with device ECAP and only secondary PROMIS pain interference, not an analgesic efficacy result. Query counts are returned-hit counts, not eligible cohorts. Keyword triage and bounded manual checks do not close systematic screening or establish linked patient data. Later dated refresh and owner access remain open.

previous_record_recheck_2026_09_25.finding: All 14 status and lastUpdatePostDateStruct values matched the audit. NCT02924129 and NCT04319887 had hasResults=true; their data availability values were corrected to distinguish aggregate results from IPD=NO and unestablished patient linkage.

primary_locators.locator: Archived capture of original BMJ publisher article, Methods > Study design and population names NCT04319887; Results opening paragraph gives 231 IPG recipients and 11 exclusions

s237_ecap_study_identity_2026_09_28.verified: The primary article explicitly identifies NCT04319887. It reports 231 implanted participants and 11 exclusions from the implant-phase analysis, leaving 220 in that article analysis; the official registry reports 300 actual enrolled in the overall registered study. These are different denominators and are not interchangeable.
s237_ecap_study_identity_2026_09_28.cross_study_boundary: NCT04319887 is a separate registered protocol from EVOKE NCT02924129. The checked public article/registries provide no shared participant identifiers or cross-enrollment statement, so individual-level zero overlap is unproven. Both registrations have aggregate results and IPD sharing NO; no open participant-keyed ECAP x pain table is established.
s237_ecap_study_identity_2026_09_28.independent_check: Root parsed the archived publisher article text for the exact NCT ID and 231/11 counts and fetched the current official ClinicalTrials.gov API record; the live BMJ route returned 403 on this check.
